question: In tuberculosis of the hip joint, the joint space is typically PRESERVED early in the disease because articular cartilage is destroyed relatively late, unlike pyogenic septic arthritis where joint space loss is an early radiological feature.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect — the statement is TRUE. The Phemister triad of TB hip: (1) juxta-articular osteoporosis, (2) peripheral erosions at bare areas, (3) gradual joint space narrowing (late). Joint space is preserved early. This distinguishes TB from pyogenic arthritis (early, rapid space loss).
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. TB of the hip (coxalgia) is avascular and slowly progressive — the synovium and caseous granuloma destroy cartilage gradually, so early radiographs show periarticular osteoporosis and soft tissue swelling with PRESERVED joint space (Phemister triad). In contrast, pyogenic arthritis rapidly destroys cartilage (proteases), causing early joint space loss within days.
